text: Dong Nai attracts more than $2.5 billion in FDI in 10M

Southern Dong Nai city attracted more than $2.5 billion in foreign direct investment (FDI) in the first 10 months of 2026, with expectation to secure more large-scale, high-tech projects in 2027, supported by infrastructure advantages, particularly Long Thanh International Airport, and plans for a free trade zone.
Industrial parks across the city continue to draw interest from major investors and businesses.

With an increasingly favourable investment environment, Dong Nai has become a manufacturing base for major foreign-invested groups, including Nestlé, C.P., Amata, Coherent, Hyosung, Bosch, Lixil, Formosa, Central Retail Vietnam and Chang Shin.

In recent months, several companies have held discussions with the management board overseeing the city's industrial and economic zones to explore investment opportunities and seek land for new manufacturing facilities.
Long Thanh High-Tech Industrial Park is among the locations attracting investor attention.

Situated alongside the Ho Chi Minh City-Long Thanh-Dau Giay Expressway, with connections to Interchange 319 and less than 10km from Long Thanh International Airport, the park benefits from convenient access to major transport networks.
Supported by synchronised infrastructure, the industrial park has attracted more than $421 million in investment from Japan, South Korea, China and other countries.
Projects are concentrated in the electrical, electronics and high-tech sectors.
Dong Nai has 89 planned industrial parks covering nearly 43,400 hectares, of which 44 are currently operational.
